# Ben Lester: selected projects

> A curated list of projects by Ben Lester, a software and systems engineer, from ideas to shipped products. It is rebuilt daily from his GitHub repositories.

- CV and contact: https://benlester.me
- GitHub: https://github.com/lester-01
- This page: https://projects.benlester.me/

## Featured

- ProxyHut (live): ProxyHut gives you real residential and mobile 4G/5G proxies from hardware you control: your broadband, modems and SIMs. A product I have built over several years. You keep the client online; ProxyHut runs the hub and relays. Free consultation and trial. GitHub home for the product; the code is not in this repo. Website: https://proxyhut.benlester.me. Code: https://github.com/lester-01/proxyhut.
- Jasiri (live): Jasiri puts an AI agent and a full Linux computer inside your Android phone. One APK shares files between chat and terminal; data stays on-device. Bring your own OpenRouter or OpenAI key. Sideload from jasiri.benlester.me—not on Google Play yet. Website: https://jasiri.benlester.me. Code: https://github.com/lester-01/jasiri.
- Jasiri apt repository (live): The public apt repository for the Jasiri Linux system, which runs on Android phones. A signed Debian-style repository at apt.benlester.me with downloadable .deb releases for aarch64 and x86_64, built and published with a Go pipeline. Add the source, run apt update, install. Website: https://jasiri.benlester.me. Code: https://github.com/lester-01/jasiri-apt.
- Fineract and Rafiki bridge (live): Case study: an Apache Fineract ledger bridged to Rafiki Open Payments so wallets move money over Interledger while the bank ledger stays source of truth. Three-bank sandbox, CI, and a short walkthrough. Write-up at fineract-rafiki.benlester.me; live sandbox on request. Website: https://fineract-rafiki.benlester.me. Code: https://github.com/lester-01/fineract-rafiki-bridge-showcase.
- SINC Student CRM (live): CRM for education agencies placing students abroad. Sales manage inquiries and chats; managers watch the application pipeline. React on Cloudflare Pages, Hono API on Workers, Supabase for auth and data. Live demo with seeded manager, sales, and client accounts. Website: https://sinc-crm.benlester.me. Code: https://github.com/lester-01/sinc_crm.
- SignalStack (finished): A realtime chat server in Go with a Next.js client, built to explore how a WebSocket server handles many concurrent connections: routing, backpressure, graceful shutdown and reconnects. Includes tests run with the race detector and a load-test harness. A systems exercise, not a chat product. Code: https://github.com/lester-01/signalstack.

## More work

- WireGuard for IoT: encryption-optional research (building): Lab research on WireGuard for constrained IoT and SBC devices that lack hardware crypto acceleration. Measures CPU and throughput when both peers optionally skip transport encryption on hops you own. PC results: about 42% lower per-packet time; fast VM tunnels show little gain. Phone and board field work still open. Lab only—not a production VPN. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- Projects command center (live): I use this private hub to inventory my GitHub repos, track status and tags, ship a portable agent kit, and publish the allowlisted public board (what-am-building / projects.benlester.me). Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- NATBridge: reverse proxy over QUIC (building): Reverse SOCKS5/HTTP relay over QUIC for hosts behind NAT. An egress dials a public relay; clients use the relay as a normal proxy while traffic exits from the egress. Go PoC with scripted iperf labs; still in active development. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- QUIC in the Linux kernel (building): C-first research toward a Linux in-kernel QUIC datapath that can match top userspace stacks on throughput while keeping kernel CPU costs low. Uses MsQuic and lxin/quic as references; includes lab benches and design notes. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- SOCKS5 server with reverse tunnel (building): Go SOCKS5 server with optional reverse-tunnel relay for TCP CONNECT and UDP ASSOCIATE. Work tool for exposing a NAT-side proxy through a public peer. Related to the socks5-reverse-tunnel* experiments. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- PTY Shuttle (building): PTY host with thin clients: spawn TUI programs (or a shell) and attach from CLI, Android, or a browser. Unix socket and WebSocket shuttles; not a cloud IDE and not an agent harness. Phases 0–3 done (host, LAN WebSocket, Android PoC); more RPC/status work planned. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- Comment moderation API (building): Small HTTP service that scores comment text with a Hugging Face sequence-classification model. Starlette/uvicorn API with local or Hub model load, plus Termux-oriented install notes. Prototype for offline-friendly moderation scoring. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- GCE spot VM provisioner (building): CLI that creates short-lived Google Compute Engine VMs for tests, batch jobs, and AI agents. Spot by default, required max run time, SSH key minting, and disks deleted with the VM so forgotten instances do not linger. Python tool (`gce-vm`); still gaining features from the roadmap. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- iperf3 through proxies (building): Fork scaffold of iperf3 with planned SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT support on the client. Meant for measuring throughput through real proxies and reverse tunnels without a separate port-forward helper. Upstream snapshot is vendored; proxy paths are still being built. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- Raspberry Pi phone-mirroring kiosk (building): Turn a Raspberry Pi OS Lite box into a phone-mirroring kiosk with Cage, scrcpy, and ADB. Modules cover a power-isolating USB Y-cable, udev attach, and a least-privilege kiosk user. Docs-first appliance build. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- Cursor Agent on Android (Termux) (live): Run the Cursor Agent CLI natively on Termux (Android ARM64) — no proot or glibc chroot. Supports the interactive TUI, login/resume, and phone-as-cloud-worker mode. Installer plus patch scripts for node-pty, SQLite, and Android tmp quirks. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- AI media search and cleanup (building): Design-first project for on-device media search and cleanup: one structured text record per photo, document or video, to find files by describing them and to spot duplicates and old versions. Done: JSON schema, validator, example data, 11 design docs. Pipeline not built yet; may become a Jasiri plug-in. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- Telegram registration bot (finished): Telegram bot written in Go that signs users up for notifications. It checks whether a Telegram account is already registered through an HTTP API, asks new users for an email address, validates it and registers them. Configured by environment variables; sending alerts is left to the backend. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.

## On hold and early ideas

- Universal EV charger adapter kit (idea): Hardware concept for a compact Type 2 / J1772 EVSE handshake adapter that extracts single-phase AC for RV and field loads (working name OAPE). Spec and architecture notes only—no PCB, firmware, or BOM checkout yet. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
- Laptop power bank (idea): Hardware blueprints for a high-density laptop power bank (Stealth Brick): 4S pack, power-path switching, Dell ID pin, and USB-C PD. Draft design notes only—no finalized BOM or enclosure CAD yet. Private repository, shown by name and summary only.
